findings.text: non-blocking: The census is described as counting "worker-written shell script" while the instrument's shell_script() accepts any file whose first two bytes are #!, so Python files (pair.py in the after depth-2 hits, check_snapshot_assertions.py in the before depth-3 hits) are counted; it inflates the depth-2 and depth-3 percentages by at most 0.5 points each and leaves the depth-1 after figure (11.0 %) above the 5 % bound, so the arm's failure stands.

non-blocking: One of the five representative census paths, r-20261123T190235235854-delivered-work-lands-without-a-coordinator-s66/gate_base.sh, no longer resolves because its run directory was pruned, so a reader cannot open it; the full recorded list survives in arms/wrapper-census2-1343925.json and run directories are transient by design.

non-blocking: The four "after" value labels are drawn in the series green #2e8b57 at 4.24:1 against the white canvas, under the 4.5:1 WCAG AA floor for 14 pt text, while the grey "before" labels beside them read 9.74:1; the bar lengths repeat the same numbers so no reader is blocked.

justifications.fit: The fragment follows the sibling evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-or-its-job-cannot-overwrite-shared-files/a-worker-or-its-job-cannot-overwrite-shared-files-s13.html and both commits carry conventional subjects with explanatory bodies and no attribution trailer.
